description: OIDC authorization request with unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to inject/override authorization parameters; verify server rejects or does not process attacker-controlled request object.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume semantic authorization parameters from an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if it accepts and processes it, proof verification is not applied to the consumed proof.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; attacker-controlled authorization parameters may be consumed without signature verification (proof integrity violation).

description: Token exchange with a clearly non-JWT / untrusted subject_token should be rejected; control flow uses a normal password login to prove the client works.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unverified/invalid subject_token as proof during token exchange; if it issues a token anyway, it consumed semantics without authentic verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed; token-exchange rejection/acceptance cannot be attributed to proof verification behavior.
Dex accepted an invalid/unverifiable subject_token during token exchange, indicating consumed proof semantics without proper verification (proof integrity violation).

description: Attempt to substitute trust anchor by enabling a connector with insecure signature validation, then perform token exchange with attacker-controlled subject_token; compare against a second connector without insecure validation.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept tokens whose signature/issuer trust anchor is attacker-controlled; if insecure validation causes acceptance, verification policy is not applied to the consumed proof semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Secure OIDC connector accepted attacker-controlled subject_token; indicates signature/issuer verification not applied to consumed proof semantics.
Connector configured to skip signature validation accepted attacker-controlled subject_token; proof integrity is violated because consumed semantics are not authenticated.

description: Direct-endpoint attack: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) to the OIDC auth endpoint and ensure it is rejected or not processed.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or process an unsigned (alg=none) JWT request object such that attacker-controlled authorization parameters are consumed without authenticity verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating request parameters may be consumed without authenticity verification (proof integrity failure).
Control OIDC auth initiation failed unexpectedly; request-object test results may be inconclusive due to client/connector misconfiguration.

description: Brokered-flow attack: obtain an ID token for one principal, then attempt to exchange it while authenticated as a different principal/client session and ensure Dex does not consume it as the wrong identity (no proof/session substitution).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind the consumed upstream proof (subject_token) to the verified principal it represents, and must not allow cross-principal substitution where a token for Alice is consumed in a Bob context without detecting the mismatch.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex consumed Alice's proof (ID token) in a different principal context and issued a session mapped to Alice (or otherwise accepted the substitution), indicating proof integrity/session substitution failure.
Control identities Alice and Bob mapped to the same downstream identity; substitution test becomes inconclusive because principals are not distinct in this environment.

description: Direct endpoint: attempt unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) to smuggle/override state+nonce and observe whether Dex accepts/uses attacker-controlled parameters without signature verification.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume authorization parameters from an unsigned request object (alg=none); if it accepts it, it would be verifying under 'no signature' while consuming attacker-controlled semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating it may consume attacker-controlled authorization parameters without proof integrity.
Control authorization request did not reach a meaningful server state; failures here suggest setup/connector issues rather than request-object signature enforcement.

description: Authorization-code replay: redeem the same auth code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected (one-time artifact anti-replay).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once; second redemption must fail.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial code redemption did not succeed; cannot attribute replay outcome to anti-replay enforcement.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay); second redemption should have been rejected.

description: Refresh-token replay: use offline_access to obtain a refresh token, then attempt to reuse the same refresh token again after a successful refresh (rotation anti-replay).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If refresh token rotation is enabled (default), an old refresh token must not be accepted after it has been used once.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial password login did not succeed; cannot evaluate refresh-token replay behavior.
Control failed: first refresh did not succeed; cannot evaluate rotation/replay behavior.
Old refresh token was accepted after being used once; refresh-token rotation/anti-replay appears broken.

description: Token-exchange freshness: perform a control token exchange with a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with an expired subject_token and ensure it is rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired upstream subject tokens (exp in the past); only fresh tokens should be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: token exchange with a valid subject_token did not succeed; expired-token result would be inconclusive (could be setup).
Dex accepted an expired subject_token during token exchange; freshness enforcement (exp) appears missing.

description: Password-grant access token replay after explicit revocation: ensure revoked session_token cannot be used at /userinfo (anti-replay within lifetime). Uses two identities to avoid single-user false positives.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Once a session/token is revoked, it must not be accepted again (revocation is an immediate freshness boundary).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Revoked session_token remained usable at /userinfo (revocation did not enforce freshness/anti-replay).
Control login failed; cannot attribute revocation behavior to freshness enforcement.

description: Authorization-code replay with a second identity control: redeem the same code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected; then perform a separate successful login for another user to prove the system is functional.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be accepted more than once, even if replayed immediately.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (code replay succeeded).

description: Token-exchange replay of the same upstream subject_token: perform a control exchange, then immediately replay the same subject_token and ensure Dex rejects if it enforces one-time use for exchanged artifacts. Includes a second identity control via password login.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If Dex treats exchanged subject_token artifacts as one-time, replaying the same subject_token should be rejected; otherwise, replay is possible within the token lifetime.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted the same subject_token in token exchange more than once (potential replay within lifetime).
Control token exchange failed; replay result cannot be attributed to anti-replay enforcement.

description: Attempt to replay/splice a one-time authorization code across a different browser session/state: obtain a code in session A, redeem it once (control), then try redeeming the same code again while having initiated a separate auth request (session B) to simulate cross-session code injection/replay.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be accepted more than once, even if an attacker tries to replay the code in a different session context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial authorization_code redemption did not succeed, so replay result is not attributable to anti-replay enforcement.

description: Attempt state-swap across two parallel OIDC auth initiations: start two auth requests with different state values, then (simulated) splice the wrong state into the completion path and ensure the resulting session is not accepted as authenticated.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authorization response must be bound to the initiating browser session via the original state value; cross-session state swapping must not yield a valid authenticated session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an authorization code in a mismatched state/session context (state-swap/cross-session splice).
State-swap attempt resulted in an authenticated session (identity established) despite broken flow coherence.

description: Attempt to redeem an authorization code without client authentication (no client_secret) and without PKCE proof, to test whether Dex incorrectly allows step-skipping / unbound code redemption.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client authentication context; exchanging a code without client auth must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemed without client authentication (client_secret) and without PKCE proof, indicating step-skipping / unbound code redemption.
Unauthenticated code redemption established a session identity, violating flow coherence.

description: Attempt to redeem an authorization code obtained for client_id=valence-test-client using a different client_id at the token endpoint (cross-client code injection/splicing). Includes a control redemption to prove the flow works.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the initiating client/session context; redeeming a code under a different client_id must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization-code exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow failures to flow-coherence enforcement.

description: Attempt to splice an authorization code into a different session context by redeeming it, then verifying that the resulting token cannot be used to read /userinfo as a different session (session binding / atomicity check).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct session/client context; tokens minted from a code must not be usable as if they belonged to a different session identity.

invariant_hypothesis: I3: If PKCE is used, the authorization code must be bound to the correct code_verifier; redeeming with a verifier from another session must be rejected (prevents cross-session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control redemption with correct verifier failed; cannot attribute wrong-verifier behavior to PKCE/session binding.
Authorization code was redeemable with a verifier from a different session, indicating cross-session splicing / flow coherence failure.

invariant_hypothesis: I3: Multi-step token exchange must be order-preserving and bound to the intended upstream connector; omitting connector_id must not be accepted (prevents step skipping / ambiguous connector selection).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed; token-exchange results may be due to environment misconfiguration rather than flow coherence.
